title: Choose the GlucoBar icon direction
question: The roll assigned Menu Bar Corner. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Menu Bar Corner
options.lineage: the top-right corner of a Mac screen, where the Reading sits beside the clock
options.thesis: The icon is a close-up of the place the product lives: a glass menu bar carrying the Reading.
options.viewport: A translucent bar across the upper squircle holds 112 and a rising Trend arrow; the clock sits below at half scale.
options.risk: Numerals blur below 32 px, so small sizes must drop to bar plus arrow; can read as a screenshot if the glass is timid.

raised.raise: Billing hierarchy: the Reading dominates and the clock is set at half its size, never equal.
State without colour: Trend is carried by the arrow's angle, so tinted and clear appearances still read.
One dominant direction: the arrow is the only diagonal in the icon.
The glass bar is a real Icon Composer layer whose overlap with the field computes its colour.

options.label: The Reading
options.lineage: the CGM lock-screen readout: number over Trend arrow
options.thesis: Just the Reading and its Trend, set large on a calm in-range green.
options.viewport: 112 centred, a horizontal Trend arrow beneath it, nothing else.
options.risk: The most familiar answer: it is what most glucose apps already look like, and green implies a medical 'in range' claim.

options.label: Split-Flap Board
options.thesis: The Reading on three flaps that clack over every five minutes; the amber lamp is the Alert.
options.viewport: Three black flaps read 112 across a steel squircle, an amber lamp top-right, a small Trend arrow below.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: a number that updates in place is exactly a polled Reading; loses on audience identification.
options.risk: Reads as a clock or travel app at a glance; flap seams vanish below 64 px.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: The menu bar's tiny Reading blown up until its pixels show: low resolution as the voice.
options.viewport: Pixel-built 112 in black on paper white, a pixel Trend arrow in signal orange-red.
options.case: Honest about scale (tiny text made huge) and holds product clarity; loses on audience identification.
options.risk: Reads retro or as a font tool; the accent can read as a warning colour.

options.label: Silk Colour Chords
options.thesis: Low, in-range and high as translucent bands whose overlaps compute new colours.
options.viewport: Three crossing bands with the Reading at their overlap.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the bands read as a chart legend, and Patients do not identify with silk.
options.kept: Real translucent overlap as structure, kept as the glass bar layer.

options.label: Double-Feature One-Sheet
options.thesis: Reading and Trend billed like two features fighting for one sheet.
options.viewport: A shouting Reading over a half-size Trend, ballyhoo in the corners.
options.case: Fuses poorly: loud and lurid where the product must stay calm until it matters.
options.risk: Alarmist tone for a health readout.
options.kept: Billing hierarchy: one thing dominates, the second at half its size.

options.label: Normalled Jackfield
options.thesis: Amber link lines on black glass, state drawn by stroke pattern.
options.viewport: A single amber lane tying the Reading to its range.
options.case: Fuses poorly: an operator's console, foreign to Patients and unreadable at icon size.
options.risk: Near-black plus one accent: the category default for 'technical'.
options.kept: State without colour: shape carries meaning.

options.label: Gravity-Rain Garden
options.thesis: Drops falling toward or away from a flower by Trend.
options.viewport: Rain bending around a black flower.
options.case: Fuses poorly: drops edge toward the banned blood-drop imagery and say nothing about a menu bar.
options.risk: Drop imagery is a brand ban.
options.kept: One dominant field of motion governs the whole frame.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A CGM trace threading a target band on a blue-teal gradient squircle.
canonCard.viewport: A wavy glucose line crossing a pale in-range band, ending in a dot.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every diabetes app and reads clinical.
